subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For systemd-managed Gateway runs, should literal provider keys in the config `env` block remain supported runtime credentials for real agent turns, or should daemon/provider docs and `models status --agent` steer users to `.env` or per-agent auth profiles instead?
rationale: Current source already applies config env during config snapshot reads while the service installer intentionally tracks literal config env keys without embedding their values, so the remaining fix depends on the intended credential and diagnostic contract.

options.title: Support config env for Gateway runtime
options.body: Keep config `env` as a supported provider-key source and add systemd/Gateway/status coverage proving real turns and diagnostics agree.

options.title: Prefer daemon-safe stores
options.body: Document `.env` or `models auth` as the durable daemon path and make `models status --agent` label config-env evidence so users do not expect unsupported service runtime auth.

options.title: Warn without changing runtime
options.body: Add a Gateway startup or doctor warning when managed env markers name keys that are not resolvable in the runtime context.

recommendation.title: Support config env for Gateway runtime
recommendation.body: Keep config `env` as a supported provider-key source and add systemd/Gateway/status coverage proving real turns and diagnostics agree.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent config-env test history make this the best available owner for choosing the config/status contract, with systemd owners reviewing implementation details.
